# Camera

- Inherits [`PVInstance`](pvinstance.md)
- Created with `Instance.new("Camera")`

The viewpoint the world is drawn from. A camera is an ordinary instance that a script creates and moves; the engine never moves it for you.

This page lists the members this class declares. Inherited members are
listed on the page of the class that declares them.

## Properties

| Name | Type | Default | Access | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `CFrame` | `CFrame` | — | read/write | The position of the camera and the direction it looks in. The camera looks along the `LookVector` of this value, which is -Z.<br><br>Set inside a render step (a function bound with `RunService:BindToRenderStep`, a `PreRender` handler, or an action whose context has `Rate = Render`), the value is drawn exactly as set in the current frame, and it becomes the value simulation code reads when the next tick starts. Set anywhere else, it takes effect at once and is drawn interpolated between ticks.<br><br>Read inside a render step, it returns the value that is being drawn. Read anywhere else, it returns the value simulation code sees. |
| `ClipPlane` | `CFrame` | — | read/write | A plane that hides everything behind it from this camera, used while `ClipPlaneEnabled` is on. The plane passes through the position of this `CFrame`; what is in front of its `LookVector` is drawn, and what is behind is not.<br><br>A mirror's camera stands behind the glass and uses the plane of the glass, so it draws the room and not the wall the mirror hangs on. `@engine/views` sets it for you. The camera must be behind the plane; if it is in front, the plane has no effect. |
| `ClipPlaneEnabled` | `boolean` | `false` | read/write | Whether `ClipPlane` is applied. |
| `FarPlane` | `number` | — | read/write | The distance to the far clip plane, in meters. Geometry beyond it is not drawn. |
| `FieldOfView` | `number` | — | read/write | The vertical field of view, in degrees. It is clamped to more than 0 and less than 180. |
| `NearPlane` | `number` | — | read/write | The distance to the near clip plane, in meters. Geometry closer than this is not drawn. A very small value reduces depth precision across the whole view, so prefer raising it to lowering it. It applies only to a perspective camera. |
| `OrthographicSize` | `number` | `10` | read/write | Half the height of what an orthographic camera shows, in meters. The width follows from the shape of the window. Change it to zoom a 2D view.<br><br>An orthographic camera draws everything from `FarPlane` behind it to `FarPlane` in front of it. Nothing shrinks with distance, so a top-down camera that stands lower than the top of a tall object still shows all of the object. |
| `Projection` | `Enum.CameraProjection` | — | read/write | Whether the camera is `Perspective`, for a 3D view, or `Orthographic`, for a 2D view. An orthographic camera ignores `FieldOfView` and shows `OrthographicSize` meters above and below the center of the view, at any distance. |
| `ViewportSize` | `Vector2` | — | read-only | The size of the area the world is drawn into, in pixels: the window in a game, or the Viewport panel in the editor. It changes when the window is resized or a phone is rotated. Use it to turn a screen position into a fraction, or to tell a tall screen from a wide one. |

## Methods

### `GetRenderCFrame(): CFrame`

Returns where this camera is drawn in the current frame, which is between its positions at the last two simulation ticks. Use it for a camera that follows this one.

It differs from `CFrame` only inside a render step: a function bound with `RunService:BindToRenderStep`, a `PreRender` handler, or an action whose context has `Rate = Render`. Everywhere else, including on a server, it returns `CFrame`.

### `ViewportPointToRay(point: Vector2): (vector, vector)`

Returns the ray that a pixel looks along, as an origin and a direction of length 1. Pass it to `Workspace:Raycast` to find what is under the pointer. For a perspective camera the ray starts at the camera and passes through the pixel; for an orthographic camera it starts at the pixel's own position and points straight ahead.

### `ViewportPointToWorld2D(point: Vector2): Vector2?`

Returns the position on the 2D plane that a pixel points at. Use it in a 2D game to compare a tap or a click with `Part2D.Position`. Returns nil when the camera looks along the plane or away from it.

### `WorldToViewportPoint(position: vector): (Vector2, number, boolean)`

Returns where a point in the world appears on screen: its position in pixels, its depth in meters in front of the camera, and whether it is on screen.

The position is measured from the top left of the area the world is drawn into, in the same units as `UIObject.AbsolutePosition` and `InputService:GetPointerPosition`. It is valid beyond the edges of the screen, so an arrow at the border can point toward an off-screen target. With a depth of 0 or less, the point is beside or behind a perspective camera and the position is meaningless.

It works for both projections. A `ScreenGui` that places elements by this position should have `ScreenInsets` off, or they are offset by the screen's cutout.
